title: Watershed pop-up event: Delivering relief, resources and real impact
summary: Entergy Arkansas in partnership with the Central Arkansas Development Council and other local service organizations, hosted a customer resource pop-up event designed to connect people with the support…
body_text: Bringing support to the heart of Little Rock On July 29, The Watershed in Little Rock was again a hub of hope for people in need. Entergy Arkansas in partnership with the Central Arkansas Development Council and other local service organizations, hosted a customer resource pop-up event designed to connect people with the support they need most. The event served 208 individuals, a powerful reflection of both the need for assistance and the impact of meeting customers where they are. As part of Entergy Arkansas’s Next Generation Arkansas strategy—specifically its Affordable Power pillar—events like this help ensure customers have access not only to reliable energy, but also to the resources and support that keep energy costs manageable. Real stories. Real impact. For many attendees, the event provided immediate and meaningful relief. Esha Mustafa shared her experience getting assistance and receiving a fan to help offset using her air conditioner: “I’m getting some assistance with this electric bill that I have. I’m really grateful for that. With these temperatures, a fan is going to be very necessary for the next couple months.” She encouraged others not to hesitate to seek help: “If you need assistance, don’t be ashamed. ” Letatiandra Harris also highlighted the importance of the support: “I came because I heard they were helping with light bills. With everything going on in the economy, that really means a lot—especially if you’re not working right now.” Her message was simple but powerful: “I just want to say thank you so much.” Powered by partnership and purpose Behind the scenes, the event was the result of strong collaboration and dedicated teamwork. Katrina Brown, Entergy Arkansas customer service manager and event organizer, emphasized the importance of partnerships: “We’re bringing resources from across the state together, working with CADC, who administers LIHEAP funding, and other organizations, to serve our community in one place.” For Brown and the team, the reward is in the impact. “The best part of my job is seeing someone feel relief—when they didn’t know how they were going to pay their bill or didn’t realize help was available. A simple thank you or a hug makes it all worth it.” She also underscored the team effort behind the event: “It takes a dedicated group of Entergy Arkansas employees working together to make these events successful.” More than assistance; a path to better health While many attendees came for bill assistance, some left with something even more critical: life-saving health insights. During the event, health screenings identified serious conditions for some participants, connecting them to care they didn’t know they needed. “You come in for one resource,” Brown said, “and you may receive something that could potentially save your life. When we say we power life, we truly mean it.” A lasting impact The Watershed pop-up event was more than a single day of service, it was a powerful example of what happens when community, compassion and commitment come together. Through the efforts of Entergy Arkansas employees, partners and volunteers, hundreds of customers found relief, comfort and critical resources, advancing the company’s commitment to Affordable Power by helping ease the financial burden of energy costs. As summer temperatures continue to rise, the impact of this event will extend far beyond the day itself, felt in cooler homes, lighter financial burdens and stronger connections across the community.

title: A Quieter Hurricane Season Doesn't Mean Lower Risk
summary: A Quieter Hurricane Season Doesn't Mean Lower Risk
body_text: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's (NOAA) latest seasonal update, issued August 6, trimmed its 2026 Atlantic hurricane forecast to seven to thirteen named storms, with zero to two reaching major strength, and put the odds of a below-normal season at 75%. A rapidly strengthening El Niño is the reason why. For facility operators along the Gulf Coast, that reads as good news. It shouldn't change what you do next. A Quiet Season Still Only Takes One Storm Storm count is a poor predictor of facility-level risk. Hurricane Andrew made landfall in 1992, a year with only six named storms total, and remains one of the costliest hurricanes in U.S. history. A below-normal season lowers the odds of any single facility taking a direct hit. It does not lower the consequences if that hit happens to be yours. The math that actually matters isn't "how many storms this year." It's "what happens to my facility if the one that forms tracks toward me." That question doesn't get easier to answer with a favorable seasonal outlook, and treating a quiet forecast as a reason to defer resilience investment gets the risk backwards. What an Outage Actually Looks Like in a Severe Storm It's worth being specific about what "unprepared" costs, because the abstraction is where facilities lose their sense of urgency. A direct hit doesn't produce a brief flicker and a quick restoration. Major hurricanes have historically knocked out power to millions of accounts for days, and in the worst-hit areas, for weeks, as utility crews work through downed transmission structures, broken poles, and damaged substations before they can even begin reconnecting individual facilities. During that window, a hospital or nursing home without sufficient backup capacity isn't managing an inconvenience, it's managing a life-safety emergency. A cold storage or food processing facility isn't losing a little inventory, it's losing the entire contents of every freezer and cooler on-site, often before a single insurance adjuster arrives. A manufacturing or distribution operation isn't delayed, it's dark for as long as the surrounding grid stays down, with no visibility into when that changes. And restoration doesn't happen evenly. Utilities prioritize hospitals, emergency services, and high-population-density areas first. A standalone commercial facility, a rural distribution center, a mid-size manufacturing plant, these are often near the back of the queue, sometimes for a week or more after the storm has passed. If your facility's survival depends on when the utility gets to you, you don't control your own timeline. That is the actual risk a quiet forecast doesn't change. The Regulatory Floor Keeps Rising Regardless of the Forecast Facility-level outage requirements haven't loosened to match a quieter seasonal outlook, and they aren't going to. Florida requires nursing homes and assisted living facilities to maintain generator power and fuel sufficient to keep safe temperatures for at least 96 hours, a standard adopted after Hurricane Irma exposed what happens when that capacity doesn't exist. California's Assembly Bill 2511 sets the same 96-hour bar for skilled nursing facilities. These mandates apply every season, independent of what NOAA forecasts in August. For hospitals, cold storage , food processing, and other facilities where an extended outage means lost product, lost revenue, or worse, the standard to meet doesn't move because the season looks calmer on paper. The Part Most Facilities Get Wrong: Backup Capacity Isn't Binary Most facilities assume they either have backup power or they don't. In practice, backup coverage exists on a spectrum, and the gap between "we have a generator" and "we can actually sustain critical operations through a multi-day outage" is where most facilities get caught off guard. Generator runtime is only as good as fuel supply, and fuel logistics fail predictably during storm events. Commercial fuel preparedness typically intensifies in the 72 hours before landfall, with retail stations running dry as residents and businesses top off simultaneously, and post-landfall fuel delivery becoming uncertain for 24 to 96 hours after a storm passes, precisely the window when a facility on generator power needs it most. A facility with a generator but no reliable fuel plan for that window has backup power in name only. Where EzFill Fits In: Fuel That Doesn't Depend on the Station Down the Street This is the exact gap EzFill was built to close. Retail gas stations are a shared, finite resource, and in the days before a storm, every business and household in the evacuation zone is drawing from the same limited supply at the same time. A facility relying on sending someone to a station to fill cans or top off a generator tank is competing with everyone else in the region for fuel that may already be gone by the time they arrive. EzFill delivers fuel directly to a facility on a scheduled or on-demand basis, independent of whether the station down the street has run dry. That means a facility can top off generator tanks and fuel reserves in the days before landfall without sending staff out to compete for supply, and can request delivery again as soon as it's safe to do so after the storm passes, rather than waiting for retail infrastructure to come back online. For a facility that has to be self-sufficient during exactly the window when local fuel supply is least reliable, that distinction is the difference between a generator that runs and one that doesn't. One Plan, Not Three Separate Ones Fuel delivery, backup generation, and battery storage are usually treated as three unrelated purchasing decisions made by three different people at three different times. That fragmentation is exactly what leaves gaps. A facility that pairs on-site battery storage with a dependable fuel plan isn't choosing one over the other, it's covering the failure modes of each. Storage doesn't depend on a delivery reaching the site during the least reliable window of the storm cycle, so it can carry critical loads through the immediate outage. A dependable fuel plan, through EzFill, keeps generators running for the extended restoration period that follows, when a storage system alone may not have enough capacity to carry a facility for days. Layered together, and managed intelligently through NextNRG's Smart Microgrid Controller , these pieces cover a period no single system covers on its own. That gap is exactly what a quieter season makes easy to ignore, since the pressure to fix it feels lower when the forecast looks favorable. But the facilities that get caught unprepared are rarely the ones that ignored an active season. They're the ones that assumed a quiet one meant they had more time. title: How to batch a month of TikTok content in one day
summary: Learn how to batch a month of TikTok content in 1 day for your brand. Streamline your workflow and scale consistency with Sprout Essentials.
body_text: Table of Contents Share Email Share Resource TikTok rewards brands that show up consistently with relevant, engaging content. But for a small business, maintaining that presence can quickly turn into a full-time production cycle. Thankfully, you don’t need to brainstorm, film and edit a new video every day. TikTok content batching helps you turn one focused production day into an entire month of posts. By grouping similar tasks, you can keep your calendar moving without scrambling for an idea every morning. Here’s how to plan, produce and schedule 20 TikTok videos in one realistic workday. What is TikTok content batching? A quick summary TikTok content batching is a high-efficiency workflow designed for solo social media managers and small businesses to script, film, edit and schedule multiple short-form videos in a single dedicated time block. Clustering similar tasks prevents creative friction, protects your bandwidth and maintains a consistent presence while freeing you up to run your business. While this playbook breaks down short-form video execution, you can scale social media content batching across your entire marketing mix. How do you map out a 30-day TikTok content calendar? A month of TikTok ideas feels more manageable when you organize them into content pillars. Pillars are themes that give each post a strategic purpose. They also keep your calendar varied so your feed doesn’t feel overly promotional or repetitive. Example: For five posts a week, divide 20 videos across four pillars: educational, behind-the-scenes, product spotlights and social proof . Content Pillar Description Frequency Example Post Idea Educational Demystify a common industry question or share a quick tip. 2x per week “3 mistakes SMBs make when launching a product.” Behind-the-scenes Humanize your brand by showing your team, workspace or daily routine. 1x per week A packaging order timelapse with a trending voiceover. Product spotlight Showcase your product/service features and real-world value. 1x per week A quick video showing “before vs. after” using your tool. Social proof Share customer success stories, testimonials and positive reviews to build trust. 1x per week Green-screening a customer email saying how much they love your brand. This framework helps you batch posts for the entire month without losing your mind inventing 20 new, unrelated ideas. It also keeps your calendar balanced: Educational content builds authority Behind-the-scenes posts make your brand feel relatable Product videos connect features to tangible value Social proof gives potential customers a reason to trust and buy from you Use the remaining days as breathing room. You can engage with comments, respond timely to trends or replace a planned post when a better opportunity pops up. Remember, batching should create flexibility, not lock your brand into a calendar you can’t touch. Sample one-day TikTok batching schedule Time Focus Output 9:00 AM – 10:30 AM (90 mins) Content pillar mapping and scripting 20 concepts, hooks and calls-to-action 10:45 AM – 1:15 PM (2.5 hours) Production sprint 20 filmed videos plus reusable B-roll 1:15 PM – 2:00 PM (45 mins) Lunch break Recharge your creative energy 2:00 PM – 4:00 PM (2 hours) Rapid editing and asset polishing 20 captioned, branded and export-ready videos 4:00 PM – 4:30 PM (30 mins) Scheduling and optimization A complete month of TikToks on your calendar What’s the step-by-step workflow to batch a month of TikToks in one day? Now let’s break down the full-day batching schedule above into realistic steps that you can follow when planning your own TikTok strategy . Step 1: The scripting strategy (9:00 AM – 10:30 AM) The first thing you need to do is map out your 20 concepts for the month. Use your content pillars to guide the mix. Don’t write word-for-word scripts for every video unless your topic requires precision (e.g. in medical, finance or scientific industries). It will help you sound more natural on camera. Write your hooks and calls-to-action (CTAs) first. They determine whether the middle of your video has direction and makes sense. Hook structures to try: “If you’re struggling with [problem], start here.” “Three things I wish I knew before [task].” “Stop doing [common mistake] if you want [outcome].” “Here’s what nobody tells you about [topic].” “Before you buy [product category], check this.” “We tested [approach]. Here’s what happened.” Additionally, keep your CTAs specific to the post. Avoid generic phrases like “follow for more”. Instead, opt for strong, actionable words, such as: “Save this checklist for your next launch.” “Comment with the step you’re stuck on.” “Send this to someone planning their next launch.” Pro tip: If you get stuck on a caption, enter at least 10 characters in Sprout Compose and use Suggestions by AI Assist to generate three alternatives. Treat those suggestions as a starting point. Edit the strongest option until it sounds exactly like your brand. Before moving into production, create a simple shot list with the title, format, props and wardrobe for each video. Consider it the final step in your scripting process. Step 2: The production sprint (10:45 AM – 1:15 PM) Now it’s time to execute your plan: filming content for 20 videos back-to-back. Film by format instead of following your content calendar. For example, you could record all your talking-head videos first, then move on to product demos, voiceovers and B-roll. You’ll spend less time changing your setup and stay in the ‘zone’ longer. More tips to make a month of content feel organic and varied: Bring four or five easy layers, such as jackets, sweaters or scarves Alternate between standing and sitting Shift the framing between close-up and medium shots Use two or three simple backgrounds Change the product or visual prop in the frame Make sure you film two takes of each hook. The opening seconds carry the most pressure, and a second option can save an otherwise strong video during editing. Once you move into the main point, prioritize clarity and energy over perfect delivery. Also, capture more B-roll than you think you need. Film hands using your product, packing an order, typing, preparing materials or moving through a routine. These clips can cover edits, add context and support future voiceover videos. Step 3: Rapid editing and asset polishing (2:00 PM – 4:00 PM) With filming complete, the most setup-heavy part of the day is behind you. After lunch, shift from production mode to editing mode and use the same process for all 20 videos. The key is to move fast. Bulk-import your clips into your video editor and organize them using the same numbering system as your scripts. Then edit in three passes: Trim: Remove false starts, long pauses and dead air Add context: Insert B-roll, screenshots or product shots where needed Polish: Add on-screen captions, cover thumbnails and brand elements Stick to one or two editing templates across the batch. Also, reuse captions, transitions and covers to save time and keep your videos consistent. If you’re adding automated TikTok captions , make sure to review them manually to catch any errors. Step 4: Automated scheduling (4:00 PM – 4:30 PM) By now, you have 20 finished videos sitting in your camera roll or TikTok drafts. Use these last 30 minutes to schedule them all for the next month. Use Sprout Social to speed up this process. Schedule your TikTok videos on a social media calendar alongside other social posts so they’re part of your larger publishing strategy. For each TikTok: Add the details: Upload a cover and write the caption, hashtags and mentions Set the timing: Select the exact time and date you want your post to go live Preview and schedule: Check the finished post before adding it to your calendar Once all 20 posts are scheduled, review the month as a complete system. Check that your pillars are balanced, the same message doesn’t appear twice in a row and promotional posts have enough value-led content around them. Then step away. Your month is ready. Upload your TikToks, organize them in a calendar view and schedule each one to automatically go live at the best possible time . You can also track the performance of your TikToks alongside other social content using Sprout’s detailed insights and cross-network reports. Essentials is built for solo marketers and small teams. It starts at an affordable price of $79 per seat per month (for up to five social media profiles). Here’s how its top features help you batch TikTok content: How do Optimal Send Times eliminate guessing? Sprout’s ViralPost® Optimal Send Times automatically calculates when your audience is most active and drops your batched content into those high-performance windows. This ensures small businesses on TikTok hit peak hours without manually publishing. How does the Publishing Calendar keep your month organized? Sprout’s collaborative calenda r brings your entire month of content into one visual view. Drop your drafted videos directly onto the calendar, and switch between month and week views to avoid accidentally scheduling identical topics back-to-back. Use Sprout’s Post Performance Report to understand how well your hooks worked. Compare your videos using metrics like TikTok video views , watch time, saves, shares, comments and engagement rate, identify patterns in your top-performing content, then use those insights to optimize your next monthly batch. Ready to make your next batching day a little easier? Let Sprout handle the scheduling and reporting so you can focus on creating content your audience loves. Creators and social teams can use Sprout Social’s Advanced Post Scheduler to plan, draft and schedule TikTok posts days or weeks in advance. This lets you map out your video calendar seamlessly from a single desktop dashboard rather than manually uploading clips from your phone every day. title: Teen Weight Loss Program — Virtual Care Led by Pediatricians
summary: A comprehensive, 100% virtual teen weight loss program led by board-certified pediatricians. Includes FDA-approved medications (Wegovy, Saxenda, Qsymia), nutrition counseling, and behavioral support for adolescents ages 12+.
body_text: Medically reviewed by: Dr. Makia Powers, MD, MPH, MSc, DABOM (Diplomate, American Board of Obesity Medicine) Last medically reviewed: August 12, 2026 A good teen weight loss program is not a diet or a quick fix. Doctors call the approach that works "intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment." In plain terms, it is a structured program that gives a family real time with a care team, ideally 26 or more hours of contact over 3 to 12 months. It works on three things together: everyday habits, healthy eating, and physical activity. The whole family takes part, and the goal is your teen's health, not just a number on the scale. This guide from Blueberry Pediatrics explains what the research really shows, how to spot a program that meets the standard, the safety questions that matter most, and when to call your child's doctor. Key takeaways The clinical name for a real teen weight loss program is "intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment," or IHBLT. Some programs call it a "family healthy weight program." The evidence-based standard is 26 or more hours of contact over 3 to 12 months. More hours tend to work better. Programs shorter than 3 months have not been shown to work. Effective programs include all three of these: behavior change, healthy eating, and physical activity. A proprietary diet is not the secret ingredient. Every program that worked in studies included the family. For teens, a good program also builds your teen's own skills and choices. Structured, professionally run programs are linked to less disordered eating. Self-guided dieting is linked to more . Good programs screen for it before, during, and after. The strongest evidence is for children ages 6 to 12. For 13-to-16-year-olds, the evidence is thinner. That is worth knowing on a page for teen parents. Medication is added to a program for some teens as an adjunct, never a replacement for it. Surgery, for a smaller group, starts with a referral for evaluation, not a decision that surgery will happen. Both come from the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) guideline. Blueberry Pediatrics' content is educational and is not medical advice. The right plan is a decision for your family and your child's doctor. What a "teen weight loss program" really is When parents search for a teen weight loss program, what they are usually looking for has a clinical name: intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, or IHBLT. It is the treatment the AAP recommends first for children and teens with overweight or obesity. You may also see it called an "intensive behavioral intervention" or a "family healthy weight program." Those are the words to search for. A real program is not a handout of health tips. It is scheduled, hands-on support from a care team over months. The AAP's own parent guidance puts it simply: "They go beyond handouts with health tips. The programs engage with your family to provide face-to-face opportunities to practice healthy behaviors." American Academy of Pediatrics, HealthyChildren.org Programs may bring in different specialists, such as dietitians, exercise specialists, and health educators. They can run inside a clinic or in a community setting. And the goal is bigger than weight. The AAP says the main goals are good health, quality of life, and self-esteem, with respect for bodies of all shapes. The 26-hour standard: the one number to remember If you carry one fact into a conversation with a program, make it this one. The most effective treatment gives a family 26 or more hours of contact over a 3-to-12-month period. Here is the AAP's guideline in its own words: "Health behavior and lifestyle treatment is more effective with greater contact hours; the most effective treatment includes 26 or more hours of face-to-face, family-based, multicomponent treatment over a 3- to 12-month period." American Academy of Pediatrics, 2023 Clinical Practice Guideline Two things make this number so useful. First, 26 hours is a floor, not a target. More contact tends to work better. Programs that deliver 52 or more hours show the most consistent results. You can see the pattern in the share of programs that produced a significant improvement, sorted by how many hours they offered: Contact hours offered Share that produced a significant BMI improvement Fewer than 5 hours About 28% 5 to 25 hours About 38% 26 hours or more About 75% Second, short programs do not clear the bar. The AAP found that "interventions lasting less than 3 months did not demonstrate effectiveness." That single line is the clearest reason to be careful with a 6-week challenge or a one-month reset. The same 26-hour standard is echoed by a separate expert group, the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force, in its 2024 recommendation. Two expert bodies reviewing this evidence landed on the same number, which is a good sign it's solid. An honest word about teens and the evidence Here is the fact most likely to be left off a page selling teen programs, and you deserve to have it. The treatment is recommended for teens and is the AAP's first choice for them. But the evidence is strongest in younger children. The AAP states the treatment effect is seen in children ages 2 to 16, "but most consistently in children 6 to 12 years of age." It points to research showing less effect in 13-to-16-year-olds than in younger kids. In plain terms: the approach is right for teens, but the deepest proof is in school-aged children. Why does this matter for choosing a program? Because finishing the hours is the hard part. Drop-out is common. That makes it smart to pick a program your teen will actually stay in and take part in, not just the one with the best pitch. What a good program includes The research points to three core parts, and they work best together. Behavior change. The family learns practical skills. Parents work on their own habits and positive parenting, and teens learn goal-setting, body acceptance, and how to handle bullying. Healthy eating. The most effective nutrition help is hands-on, like real meal prep and tasting, not just a lecture. Importantly, no single diet has been shown to beat the others. A proprietary meal plan is not the active ingredient. Physical activity. A mix of activity types works better than advice alone. The best programs make movement fun and doable, and adapt it to your child. Good programs also use a coaching style called motivational interviewing. Instead of telling your teen what to do, the care team helps your teen find their own reasons to change. A program that just hands your teen a list of rules is using an older approach the AAP has moved away from. One honest caution. Many good programs also cover sleep, screen time, and weight stigma. Those are healthy things to address. But the AAP is clear that these extras have not been shown to add measured benefit to the core treatment. They are signs of a caring program, not the reason a program works. Family involvement, and what it means for a teen Every program that worked in the studies included the parent or the family. Programs that treat the teen alone, like some school or camp programs, are outside the evidence base. So family involvement is not optional. But "family-based" does not mean "parent-run." The AAP is candid that, for teens, the best way to involve parents is less clear than it is for young children. Studies with teens focus more on the teen's own choices, preferences, and self-image. The practical takeaway for a parent of a 15-year-old: a strong program builds your teen's own skills and independence while keeping the home environment in the picture. That balance is a real sign of a program designed for teens. Safety first: eating disorders and your teen This is the fear many parents carry, and it is the most important part of this page. The good news is backed by strong evidence. Structured, professionally run programs are linked to less disordered eating, not more. The AAP is unusually direct here: "…participation in structured, supervised weight management programs decreases current and future eating disorder symptoms … up to 6 years after treatment." American Academy of Pediatrics, 2023 Clinical Practice Guideline The reason makes sense: a good obesity program and an eating-disorder program share a lot. Both build healthy eating, movement for enjoyment, and self-esteem. One key point, though. This protection is tied to structured, supervised, professional care. It does not transfer to an unsupervised app, a commercial product, or a parent-run diet at home. In fact, self-guided dieting is linked to more disordered eating and even more weight gain over time. One boundary on this evidence: the studies behind it did not include teens who already had a diagnosed eating disorder or mental-health condition. If that describes your teen, this is a conversation to have with your child's doctor before starting any program, not a reason to avoid care, but a reason to plan it together. That is why screening matters. A quality program checks for signs of disordered eating before, during, and after treatment, and watches for weight coming off faster than expected. Ask any program how they do this. It is one of the sharpest questions you can ask. Warning signs to watch for Call your child's doctor if you notice severe food restriction, skipping meals to lose weight, self-induced vomiting, or use of diet pills or laxatives. Other signs include compulsive exercise, social withdrawal, a strong fear of gaining weight, or a distorted body image. Rapid weight loss or a sudden drop on the growth chart also deserves a call. This list comes from the AAP's guidance on preventing eating disorders in teens. A note on how you talk about weight at home matters too. Research shows that when families talk about weight and dieting, teens are more likely to diet in unhealthy ways. When the conversation is about healthy eating and being active to feel good, teens do better. So keep the focus on health and habits, not the scale. Where medication and surgery fit For some teens, a doctor may add medication or, less often, refer for a surgical evaluation. These are rungs on the same ladder as the program, not competing choices. The AAP's framing is important: medication is an "adjunct" to a lifestyle program, never a replacement for it. And the program should not stop once a medicine starts. For teens 12 and older who have obesity, a doctor may offer weight-loss medication alongside the program. For teens 13 and older with severe obesity, a doctor may refer for a surgical evaluation. A referral is an evaluation and a conversation, not a decision that surgery will happen. This page is about the program. For a full, plain-language look at the medicines themselves (which ones are FDA-approved for teens, how they work, side effects, and cost), see our companion guide: Weight Loss Medication for Teenagers: A Parent's Guide . Program or product? How to tell the difference Search "teen weight loss program" and you will land on a mix of real clinical programs, diet products, apps, camps, and online offers. Telling them apart is the most useful skill on this page. Start with what the research rules out: Very short programs. Anything under 3 months has not been shown to work. A "secret" diet. No single diet beats the others. If a product sells its meal plan as the magic, the science does not back that. Teen-only programs. If the family is left out, it is outside the evidence. Now, a word about ads and testimonials. You will often see before-and-after stories. Here is a fair test you can use. Under U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) endorsement rules (16 CFR Part 255), a weight-loss testimonial claiming big results should come with a clear statement of how much weight people typically lose. The FTC also says a vague line like "results not typical" is not enough. So if a program shows dramatic testimonials but will not tell you the typical result, treat that as a red flag. One more thing worth knowing. The FTC keeps a well-known list of seven "gut check" weight-loss claims that experts say simply cannot be true, like losing weight with no diet or exercise, or from a patch or cream. That list applies to products such as supplements, pills, and skin creams, not to programs. It is a handy filter for the supplement ads that show up next to a program search, so keep it in your back pocket for those. How to find a real program, and what to ask Real programs exist, but they can be hard to find, and the honest truth is that many families face real barriers. The AAP notes that high-quality programs are scarce in many areas, and that treatment is time-intensive and often not well covered by insurance. There is a recognized quality standard to look for. The CDC recognizes a set of "family healthy weight program" models that meet the evidence bar, including the 26-hour standard. These are program models your pediatrician or health system may offer under a local name, not a directory to search by yourself. The best move is to ask your child's doctor whether a program you are considering is one of these models, or is built on the same evidence. And if there is no program near you, the AAP's own fallback is reassuring: you and your pediatrician can work through the same lifestyle and behavior topics step by step at the office. You do not have to find a commercial substitute. Here is a short checklist you can bring to any program. (This is Blueberry's own list, built from trusted guidelines.) Hours: Does it offer 26 or more contact hours over 3 to 12 months? Family: Is my family involved, and for a teen, does it also build my teen's own skills and choices? All three parts: Does it cover behavior change, healthy eating, and physical activity? Safety screening: Does it screen for disordered eating before, during, and after? Medical check-ins: Is there a medical component, like checking blood pressure and labs when needed? Cost and after: What does it cost, what does insurance cover, and what happens when the program ends? Your pediatrician: Does it connect with or loop in your child's own doctor? Evidence-based: Is it built on the AAP guideline or a recognized program model? No shame: Does it focus on health and self-esteem, not just a number, and avoid shaming your teen? If a program cannot answer these, that is your signal to keep looking. A note on virtual and telehealth programs Many families ask about online or telehealth programs, and it is a fair question for a busy household. Here is the honest picture. The AAP measures the dose in contact hours, and its strongest evidence comes from face-to-face care. It treats virtual delivery as a separate channel where the evidence is still growing, promising but not yet as established as in-person. Our own read is that a live video visit with a clinician is real contact in a way that a video library or an app on its own is not. But that is our reading, not a finding the guideline states. So the useful question is not "online or not?" It is: does this program give my teen scheduled, live time with a real care team, with my family involved? That is the standard that matters, whether the visits happen in a clinic or over video. The bottom line If your teen is carrying extra weight, know this: obesity is treated as a long-term medical condition, effective treatment exists, and it takes real time. The goal is health, not a number, and no one should be shamed into or out of care. A real program gives a family 26 or more hours over 3 to 12 months, involves the family, covers behavior, eating, and activity together, screens for disordered eating, and connects with your pediatrician. Anything that cannot meet that standard is worth walking away from. Call your child's doctor if your teen shows signs of disordered eating, sudden or rapid weight loss, new or worsening mood changes, or thoughts of self-harm. And bring your questions. A good care team welcomes them. Blueberry Pediatrics' content is for education only. It is not a substitute for advice from your child's own doctor. The right choice depends on your teen's health, history, and goals. Only you and your clinician can decide that together. Wondering what a real program should look like for your teen? Talk to a Blueberry pediatrician Frequently asked questions What is a teen weight loss program, really? The clinical name is intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, or IHBLT. It is a structured program that gives a family scheduled time with a care team, ideally 26 or more hours over 3 to 12 months, and it works on everyday habits, healthy eating, and physical activity together. It is not a diet or a quick fix. How many contact hours should a good program offer? The most effective treatment gives a family 26 or more hours of contact over a 3-to-12-month period. More hours tend to work better, and programs shorter than 3 months have not been shown to work. Is a program safe for a teen who may be at risk for an eating disorder? Structured, professionally run programs are linked to less disordered eating, not more, when the care is supervised. That protection does not transfer to an unsupervised app, a commercial product, or a parent-run diet. One boundary: the studies behind this finding did not include teens who already had a diagnosed eating disorder or mental-health condition, so if that describes your teen, talk with your child's doctor before starting any program. A quality program screens for disordered eating before, during, and after. Do online or telehealth programs count? What counts is scheduled, live time with a real care team, with your family involved. The strongest evidence in the guideline is for face-to-face care, and the AAP describes the evidence for virtual delivery as growing. Our own read is that a live video visit with a clinician is real contact in a way that a video library or an app on its own is not - but that is our reading, not a finding the guideline states. Where do medication and surgery fit? For some teens, a doctor may add medication as an adjunct to the program, never a replacement for it, and for a smaller group may refer for a surgical evaluation. Both come from the AAP guideline. This page is about the program itself; for the medicines, see our companion guide for teens and families. Sources American Academy of Pediatrics. title: Psicologia do consumo: O que faz um cliente decidir comprar online?
summary: Venda produtos físicos ou digitais com o checkout líder em conversão e gateway integrado da Cartpanda. Escale suas vendas online em 150+ países.
body_text: Por que algumas pessoas entram em um site e saem sem comprar nada, enquanto outras finalizam a compra em minutos? A resposta está na psicologia do consumo! Se você tem um e-commerce, entender o que passa na cabeça do consumidor pode fazer toda a diferença para aumentar suas vendas. Bora mergulhar nesse assunto e descobrir como influenciar as decisões de compra do seu cliente? O que é psicologia do consumo? A psicologia do consumo estuda os fatores que levam uma pessoa a tomar decisões de compra. Isso inclui emoções, experiências passadas, influência social e até mesmo detalhes sutis do site onde ela está comprando. Cada clique, cada tempo de espera e cada cor usada na sua página pode impactar se o cliente vai finalizar a compra ou desistir. No e-commerce, esses fatores são ainda mais importantes, já que o cliente não pode pegar o produto na mão ou conversar com um vendedor cara a cara. É por isso que entender como o consumidor pensa é essencial para criar uma estratégia de vendas eficiente. O que influencia um cliente na hora da compra? Se liga em alguns dos principais fatores que fazem um cliente decidir entre comprar ou abandonar o carrinho: Urgência e escassez: Promoções por tempo limitado ou estoque reduzido geram aquela pressão psicológica para não perder a oportunidade. Confiança na loja: Depoimentos, avaliações positivas e selos de segurança ajudam a passar credibilidade. Facilidade de navegação: Se o site é complicado ou demorado, o cliente desiste rápido. Preço e condições de pagamento: Frete grátis, parcelamento e descontos fazem a diferença. Atendimento e suporte: Um chat rápido ou um WhatsApp acessível deixam o cliente mais seguro para comprar. Gatilhos mentais para utilizar na hora da venda Agora que você já sabe o que influencia o cliente, é hora de usar algumas estratégias para potencializar suas vendas. Se liga nesses gatilhos mentais que podem ser aplicados no seu e-commerce: Prova social: Mostrar quantas pessoas compraram ou deixar avaliações visíveis ajuda o cliente a confiar no seu produto. Reciprocidade: Dê algo de graça (como um e-book ou desconto na primeira compra) e aumente as chances de conversão. Escassez: Exiba mensagens como "últimas unidades" ou "promoção por tempo limitado" para incentivar a decisão rápida. Autoridade: Se seu site tem certificação, selos ou influencers que já usaram seu produto, mostre isso! Facilidade: Botões claros, checkout rápido e informações diretas fazem o cliente confiar mais e comprar sem medo. Conclusão A psicologia do consumo é um dos pilares do sucesso de qualquer e-commerce. Entender como o cliente pensa e tomar decisões estratégicas para influenciar sua compra pode ser o diferencial que coloca sua loja na frente da concorrência. E aí, vamos aplicar essas estratégias e turbinar suas vendas?

summary: LEXINGTON, Mass., Aug. 03, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Keros Therapeutics, Inc. (“Keros” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: KROS), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing novel therapeutics to treat a wide range of patients with disorders that are linked to
body_text: LEXINGTON, Mass., Aug. 03, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Keros Therapeutics, Inc. (“Keros” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: KROS), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing novel therapeutics to treat a wide range of patients with disorders that are linked to dysfunctional signaling of the transforming growth factor-beta (“TGF-ß”) family of proteins, today provided a business update and reported financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. “We are excited to have initiated our Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating the treatment of rinvatercept in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (“DMD”), marking an important milestone in the development of our program,” said Jasbir S. Seehra, Ph.D., President and Chief Executive Officer. “In our Phase 1 clinical trial in healthy volunteers, rinvatercept demonstrated robust pharmacological activity observed through increases in muscle mass and bone mineral density, alongside a decrease in fat mass. We look forward to the progression of the Phase 2 clinical trial, and continue to expect to present initial data in the first half of 2027.” Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Keros reported a net loss of $28.7 million in the second quarter of 2026 as compared to a net loss of $30.7 million in the second quarter of 2025. The decrease of $2.0 million was primarily due to revenue recognized in 2025 related to Keros' license agreement with Takeda and decreased research and development efforts. Research and development expenses were $22.3 million for the second quarter of 2026 as compared to $43.5 million for the same period in 2025. The decrease of $21.2 million was primarily due to the transition of elritercept-related research and development expenses to Takeda and the corporate restructuring that was completed in 2025. General and administrative expenses were $8.6 million for the second quarter of 2026 as compared to $14.5 million for the same period in 2025. The decrease of $5.9 million was primarily due to a decrease in professional fees and a decrease in compensation costs in connection with the 2025 corporate restructuring. Keros’ cash and cash equivalents as of June 30, 2026 was $257.6 million compared to $287.4 million as of December 31, 2025. Based on current operating assumptions, Keros expects that its cash and cash equivalents as of June 30, 2026 will enable Keros to fund its operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements into the first half of 2028. About Keros Therapeutics, Inc. Keros is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing novel therapeutics to treat a wide range of patients with disorders that are linked to dysfunctional signaling of the TGF-ß family of proteins. Keros is a leader in understanding the role of the TGF-ß family of proteins, which are master regulators of the growth, repair and maintenance of a number of tissues, including skeletal muscle, bone, adipose, heart tissue and blood. By leveraging this understanding, Keros has discovered and is developing protein therapeutics that have the potential to provide meaningful and potentially disease-modifying benefit to patients. Keros’ lead product candidate, rinvatercept, is being developed for the treatment of DMD and for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Keros’ most advanced product candidate, elritercept, is being developed for the treatment of cytopenias, including anemia and thrombocytopenia, in patients with myelodysplastic syndrome and in patients with myelofibrosis. Because such statements are subject to risks and uncertainties, actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by such forward-looking statements. These risks and uncertainties include, among others: Keros’ limited operating history and historical losses; Keros’ ability to raise additional funding to complete the development and any commercialization of its product candidates; Keros’ dependence on the success of its product candidates, rinvatercept and elritercept; that Keros may be delayed in initiating, enrolling or completing any clinical trials; competition from third parties that are developing products for similar uses; Keros’ ability to obtain, maintain and protect its intellectual property; and Keros’ dependence on third parties in connection with manufacturing, clinical trials and preclinical studies. These and other risks are described more fully in Keros’ filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”), including the “Risk Factors” section of the Company’s Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q, filed with the SEC on May 14, 2026, and its other documents subsequently filed with or furnished to the SEC. All forward-looking statements contained in this press release speak only as of the date on which they were made. Except to the extent required by law, Keros undertakes no obligation to update such statements to reflect events that occur or circumstances that exist after the date on which they were made. title: Back to School: The Essential Student Tech Checklist for 2026
summary: Our back-to-school student tech checklist for 2026 covers storage, USB-C hubs, keyboards, webcams, headsets, and cooling picks from Newegg.
body_text: New semester, new setup. Whether you are heading to a dorm, a shared apartment, or logging in from your childhood bedroom, the right gear makes the difference between a smooth term and a string of last-minute panics. A modern laptop is a great start, but it rarely comes with everything a student actually needs day to day. This checklist walks through six practical upgrades, one category at a time, so you can build out a reliable, budget-friendly setup without overspending. Grab what you need, skip what you do not, and start the year ready for anything. Why a tech checklist beats impulse buying It is easy to arrive on campus, realize your new laptop only has a couple of USB-C ports, and panic-buy the first accessory you spot. A checklist flips that script. By thinking through how you actually study, submit assignments, and attend class before you shop, you buy fewer things and use them more. The goal here is not the flashiest desk setup on social media. It is a dependable kit that protects your work, keeps you comfortable during long study sessions, and makes you look and sound professional in online classes and group calls. Every pick below is available at Newegg, with prices checked on August 6, 2026. Back up your work (portable storage) Nothing ruins a semester faster than a lost final paper. Cloud storage helps, but a physical backup you control is the safety net every student should have. A portable SSD copies gigabytes of notes, photos, and project files in seconds and slips into any bag. Our pick is the Samsung T7 Portable SSD 1TB , $229.00 at the time of writing. It is compact, shock-resistant with no moving parts, and fast enough to edit video or run a portable app library straight off the drive. Set a weekly reminder to drag your coursework folder onto it, and a spilled coffee or a dead laptop becomes an inconvenience instead of a catastrophe. Keep a backup drive in your bag so your coursework travels with you. Expand your ports (USB-C hubs) Thin-and-light laptops look great until you need to plug in a monitor, a flash drive, and a charger at the same time. A USB-C hub turns a single port into many, adding HDMI, USB-A, card readers, and pass-through charging. If you are on a tight budget, the Rosewill 8-in-1 USB-C Hub (4K HDMI) delivers 4K HDMI output and a stack of extra ports for just $29.99 at the time of writing, which is hard to beat for dorm-room duty. If you want something built to last through four years and beyond, the Belkin 7-Port USB-C Hub , $62.99 at the time of writing, offers a sturdier build and reliable performance for a permanent desk setup. Not sure which fits your laptop? Browse the full range of USB-C hubs to compare ports and price. Comfortable typing (keyboard + mouse) Typing every assignment on a cramped laptop keyboard is fine for a while, and then your wrists start to complain. A full-size wireless keyboard and mouse transform any dorm desk into a comfortable workstation, and they free up screen space by letting you prop your laptop on a stand. The Logitech MK270 Wireless Keyboard + Mouse Combo , $29.99 at the time of writing, is an affordable, no-fuss choice: it uses a single tiny USB receiver, runs for months on its included batteries, and includes handy shortcut keys. It is the kind of upgrade you stop noticing precisely because it just works. Show up on camera (webcam) The Logitech Brio 100 delivers crisp 1080p video for online classes. Online lectures, virtual office hours, and remote group projects are part of student life now, and most built-in laptop cameras are grainy and unflattering. A dedicated webcam is the single easiest way to look more professional on a call. The Logitech Brio 100 1080p Webcam , $29.99 at the time of writing, delivers a crisp Full HD image, better low-light handling than most laptop cameras, and a built-in privacy shutter so you control exactly when you are seen. Clip it to your monitor and you will present clearly whether you are defending a thesis or just checking in with a study group. Sound good on calls (headset) Good audio is half of every video call, and it is the half people notice most. A proper headset cuts out roommate noise, keeps your microphone close to your mouth, and lets you focus during long study blocks. The Razer BlackShark V2 X Headset , $54.99 at the time of writing, is a lightweight, comfortable over-ear option with a clear microphone and cushioned earcups you can wear for hours. It is just as happy carrying you through a late-night gaming session as it is keeping a group presentation crisp and intelligible. Keep your laptop cool The Razer laptop cooling pad boosts airflow for demanding sessions. Heavy multitasking, video calls, and marathon research sessions push laptops hard, and heat is the enemy of both performance and battery lifespan. When a laptop runs hot, it slows itself down to protect its components, which means slower everything right when you need speed. A cooling pad lifts the chassis for better airflow and adds fans to pull heat away. The Razer Laptop Cooling Pad (14″-18″) , $129.99 at the time of writing, fits most modern laptops, raises the screen to a more ergonomic angle, and helps your machine stay quick and quiet under load. It is a worthwhile investment if you run demanding software or simply want your laptop to last through graduation. Your quick-reference checklist Build your kit one line at a time, and do not feel you need everything at once. Start with a backup drive to protect your work, add a hub so you can plug in whatever campus throws at you, then layer in comfort and communication gear as your budget allows. Here is the full checklist at a glance: Category Recommended pick Price (at time of writing) Portable storage Samsung T7 Portable SSD 1TB $229.00 USB-C hub (budget) Rosewill 8-in-1 USB-C Hub $29.99 USB-C hub (premium) Belkin 7-Port USB-C Hub $62.99 Keyboard + mouse Logitech MK270 Combo $29.99 Webcam Logitech Brio 100 1080p $29.99 Headset Razer BlackShark V2 X $54.99 Cooling pad Razer Laptop Cooling Pad $129.99 Tick these boxes and you will spend less time troubleshooting and more time learning. A dependable setup pays for itself in saved stress across a full academic year. Read More RTINGS webcam reviews — Independent, lab-tested comparisons to help you judge webcam image quality. title: Tuya Smart Unlocks Greater Value of Matter and Zigbee with an Open Ecosystem | news | Tuya Smart
body_text: Tuya Smart (NYSE: TUYA, HKEX: 2391), a global AI cloud platform service provider, made an official statement that it fully supports the integration of standard Zigbee 3.0 and Matter devices while enabling Tuya’s customized Zigbee 3.0 and standard Matter devices to connect to third-party ecosystems. This means that Tuya not only supports integration with standard protocols but allows the standard components of Tuya’s customized Zigbee 3.0 and Matter protocols to integrate into other Zigbee 3.0 and Matter hub ecosystems. This approach is consistent with Tuya’s long-standing strategy of building an open and neutral smart ecosystem. As a board member of the Connectivity Standards Alliance (CSA), Tuya Smart has always been an active advocate and practitioner of protocol standards such as Matter. It provides developers with integrated hardware and software solutions covering multiple connectivity protocols, helping them reduce Matter certification costs and shorten the time from product development and launch to market. Meanwhile, Tuya integrated hardware and software solutions cover over 20 product categories, including Matter gateways, smart sockets (metered and non-metered), switches, lighting, ceiling fan lights, sensors, curtains, smart locks, and robot vacuum cleaners. As of June 2025, Tuya has obtained 366 Matter certificates, and millions of its devices have been deployed globally in apartments, hotels, and residential households. 01 Tuya Smart: Openness as a Principle, Customization as Value Enhancement Tuya Smart’s protocol strategy features strong flexibility and openness: it not only supports the integration of standard protocols such as Matter/Zigbee, but also provides paid customized protocols to meet developers’ advanced needs for full-lifecycle management, enhanced functions, and Tuya’s interconnection ecosystem. Simply put, Tuya’s customized Matter/Zigbee 3.0 protocol is a "value-added option" built on the foundation of standard protocols. This solution retains compatibility with standard protocols while adding Tuya’s proprietary extended functions. Through Product Identification (PID), Tuya continuously supports developers in the full-lifecycle management of devices—from activation and upgrading to operation and maintenance—ensuring universality while providing enhanced solutions for developers’ scenario-specific needs. PID serves as the unique identifier of devices within Tuya’s ecosystem, empowering developers to design differentiated products and achieve efficient full-lifecycle management. Additionally, choosing Tuya’s customized Matter/Zigbee 3.0 protocol allows devices to natively integrate Tuya’s robust security capabilities. 02 Ecosystem Empowerment: Tuya’s Customized Protocol Enables Developers to Build Growth Engines For developers, except the standard Matter/Zigbee protocol, why are they still willing to pay for Tuya’s customized Matter / Zigbee 3.0 protocol? The answer lies in that Tuya’s customized Matter/Zigbee 3.0 enables developers to seamlessly access Tuya’s global open ecosystem and gain significant commercial empowerment. In terms of ecosystem empowerment, Tuya’s "Powered by Tuya" interconnection system has become a "passport" for smart devices going global. This means that smart products developed based on Tuya’s protocols can achieve cross-platform interconnection without requiring valuable R&D resources to adapt to different ecosystems such as Apple Home, Google Home and Amazon Alexa. This significantly lowers barriers to global market expansion, shortens time-to-market, and enhances market competitiveness. The advantages of Tuya’s ecosystem empowerment have been demonstrated by many overseas enterprises. Take Yooksmart, a pioneer in the smart sunshade industry, as an example. By adopting Tuya’s full-stack Matter solutions, Yooksmart not only addressed product compatibility issues with major ecosystems in Europe and North America, but also successfully entered the North American and European markets with its rich scenario-based functions. In terms of technical implementation, Tuya’s customized Tuya Matter/Zigbee 3.0 protocol brings significant product function enhancements, helping developers build differentiated competitive advantages. For example, developers can utilize Tuya to add scenario-based smart functions such as music rhythm sync and biological rhythm for lighting devices; enhance interactive experiences for switch products by adding backlight control and scheduled timing; achieve sub-second device network pairing through optimization, greatly improving user experience; and innovatively implement long data packet segmentation technology, supporting data transmission for complex scenarios like infrared and weather. These distinctive features enable products to gain differentiated competitive advantages beyond basic interoperability. Furthermore, Tuya’s ecosystem provides developers with end-to-end empowerment covering hardware development, Matter/Zigbee certification, mass production support, and deployment. Especially for enterprise deployment needs, Tuya additionally offers customized App and device firmware development, significantly enhancing user experience in scenarios such as smart homes, smart hotels, and smart apartments. This one-stop service allows developers to focus on product differentiation and innovation rather than underlying technology adaptation. More importantly, the scale of Tuya’s ecosystem has created a positive feedback loop. Data generated by the large volume of devices continuously feeds back into protocol optimization—this means that choosing Tuya’s customized Matter/Zigbee protocol not only provides access to cutting-edge technical support but also allows developers to join an intelligent ecosystem with continuous evolution capabilities. Looking ahead, Tuya Smart will continue to uphold openness and neutrality, evolving in collaboration with global developers. In Tuya’s view, true interconnection encompasses not only technical standardization but also providing developers with multiple paths from "standard compatibility" to "exceptional value". As the Matter/Zigbee standard continues to evolve, Tuya will leverage its robust open ecosystem and technological expertise to help global developers overcome ecosystem barriers, focus on innovation itself, and jointly build a smarter and more seamlessly connected future.
